name: night_pursuit_cinematic
character: A film chase cue judged as a build-hit-release piece: a motif on the horns that changes at every camera, a pulse that never stops and one slow-motion jump; it starts as `cinematic` and changes nothing until a render measures a reason.

focus.label: a line the ear can follow
focus.reason: this type is defined by a figure, so a piece that declares it must carry one; the same list means a lead or a vocal is checked exactly like a melody

channel.bars.reason: The cue's front/back balance moves by several dB from bar to bar by design: the camera-cut hits (a taiko and a rear cymbal crash at each cut) and a siren that circles behind the listener decay into the next bar. Measured on the 8-channel render (bars 21-27, 36-46 s): front-to-back energy +10.0, +10.5, +10.8, +15.7, +10.1, +12.9, +11.4 dB; the row flagged bar 24 at +5.2 dB against the 4 dB limit (+12.8 dB against +7.6 dB in both neighbours), the dip after the hit at bar 23. The limit is 6 dB, within the row's range of 1-12; every other per-bar test of the row (jump, dropout, polarity) keeps its default.
